ESA Ariane 5 media kit - ECA launch vehicle — dimensions

Ariane 5 was the heavy-lift workhorse that carried European spaceflight to its peak — after one of the most famous failures in the field. Its 1996 maiden flight self-destructed 37 seconds up when guidance software inherited from Ariane 4 overflowed at the new rocket's higher speed, a software-engineering cautionary tale now taught worldwide. It recovered to become one of the most reliable heavy launchers ever built, lofting Rosetta, Galileo (navigation constellation), BepiColombo, the ATV freighters to the ISS, and finally the James Webb Space Telescope — placed so precisely it saved years of the observatory's fuel.
ESA’s long-running heavy lifter, retired in 2023 after 117 launches. Carried Rosetta to comet 67P, JWST to L2, and dual-manifested geostationary commercial payloads for two decades.
First European spacecraft to reach the Moon; first mission to reach the Moon under ion propulsion
First spacecraft to orbit a comet — and to land on one (Philae, 2014-11-12)
First Europe + Japan joint planetary mission; second-ever spacecraft to orbit Mercury (after Messenger)
Largest interplanetary spacecraft built in Europe; first spacecraft ever to orbit a moon of another planet (Ganymede, 2034)
First European Moon mission — solar-electric ion drive. Spiralled to the Moon over 13 months; deliberate impact 2006-09-03
First spacecraft to orbit a comet (67P)
Twin-orbiter joint ESA + JAXA Mercury mission — splits into MPO + Mio at Mercury arrival in 2026
ESA flagship to Jupiter — first orbiter ever to settle around a Galilean moon (Ganymede, 2034)
China's GTO workhorse — Chang'e lunar landers + most Chinese comsats
Successor to Proton-K; modernised heavy lift
